minutes.headline: Board removed the Mass Ave land purchase and ROFR placeholders from the warrant and waived first refusal on three parcels.
minutes.summary: Remote Select Board meeting during COVID-19. Board approved two stop signs, heard the FY2019 audit (clean opinion), and heard a Community Preservation Act presentation for the ballot with no vote. It removed several placeholder articles from the town meeting warrant, waived first refusal on three Chapter 61 parcels, kept one open, and the town manager outlined plans to rework the FY21 budget.

what_happened.line: The Select Board removed the warrant article for purchasing 635 Mass Ave; the vote passed with one no vote.
The board removed four right-of-first-refusal placeholder articles from the town meeting warrant.
The board chose not to exercise first refusal on three Chapter 61 properties, and kept the Holman Street/Northfield Road parcel open pending attorney clarification.
Auditors presented the FY2019 audit with a clean opinion, flagging old outstanding checks and aged ambulance receivables to address.
The board approved two additional stop signs by unanimous roll call, and heard a Community Preservation Act presentation with no vote taken.

why_it_matters: Waiving first refusal on Chapter 61 land lets those parcels move to private sale without the town buying them, and removing the Mass Ave article means voters will not be asked to fund that purchase at town meeting.
A Community Preservation Act surcharge would be a new charge on property tax bills if voters approve it on the ballot, and the board's vote on whether to put it there is still to come.
The town manager said the FY21 budget may be reworked and the abatements and exemptions allowance could be reduced to free money for operations, which bears on next year's services and tax bill.
watch_next: Board action next week on the local option to delay property tax payments to June 1.
A Community Preservation Act ballot vote sometime in April, ahead of the ballot deadline.
